Net profit for the period refers to the net earnings attributable to owners, ultimately realized through operating, investing, and financing activities within a specific accounting period. It is the balance of total profit minus income tax expense, serving as a key indicator for measuring a company's final profitability and the final line item on the income statement.

Net profit for the period refers to the final operating result of an enterprise within a specific accounting period, calculated as total profit minus income tax expense. It is a key indicator for measuring corporate profitability and directly constitutes the major component of the increase in shareholders' equity for the period.

name: Net Profit for the Year
definitions: Net profit for the year refers to the final operating result generated by an enterprise through operating activities, investment activities, and non-recurring items within a complete fiscal year. It is the net amount after deducting all costs, expenses, taxes, and losses from total revenue, serves as the basis for profit distribution, and is classified as an owners' equity account.

Net profit for the year refers to the total profit attributable to the owners of the enterprise in the current accounting year, after deducting all costs, expenses, and taxes, generated through operating activities, investing activities, and financing activities.

name: Net Profit in the Final Period of the Forecast Horizon
definitions: Net profit in the final period of the forecast horizon refers to the projected net profit amount expected to be achieved in the last forecast period (e.g., the final year) within a specified forecast timeframe (such as the next 3, 5, or 10 years) in a corporate financial forecast or valuation model. It reflects the company's operating results at the end of the forecast period and serves as a critical input data point for calculating terminal value or discounting cash flows.

name: Net Profit or Loss from Sale of Business Property
definitions: Net profit or loss from the sale of business property represents the taxable gain or deductible loss computed as the excess of the gross sales price over the property’s adjusted cost basis (purchase cost less accumulated depreciation), reported on IRS Form 4797.

name: Net Property Income
definitions: Net property income refers to the net income received by households or enterprises for surrendering the use of their financial assets, non-financial assets, and natural resources to other institutional units, households, or individuals, after deducting related expenses. It is one of the important components of disposable income and reflects the net return from property-related activities.

name: Net Property, Plant, and Equipment (Net PP&E)
definitions: Net PP&E represents the carrying amount of tangible fixed assets on the balance sheet, calculated as gross PP&E plus capital expenditures minus accumulated depreciation. It indicates the net book value of property, plant, and equipment after recognizing investment in assets and the wear-and-tear costs through depreciation.

name: Net Realizable Value
definitions: Net realizable value refers to the net value obtained by subtracting the estimated costs to completion, estimated selling expenses, and relevant taxes from the estimated selling price of inventory in the ordinary course of business. It is a key measurement attribute for impairment testing under the lower of cost or market method for inventory.

Net realizable value refers to the estimated selling price of an asset (typically inventory) in the ordinary course of business, minus the estimated costs, expenses, and relevant taxes necessary to complete the sale. It reflects the net cash inflow expected to be realized from the asset in its current condition.

name: Net Realizable Value (NRV)
definitions: Net realizable value is the estimated selling price of an asset in the ordinary course of business minus the estimated costs of completion and the costs necessary to make the sale, commonly applied in inventory valuation and the assessment of accounts receivable to reflect a conservative measure of current asset value.

name: Net Receivables
definitions: Net receivables represent the realizable value of accounts receivable after deducting the allowance for doubtful accounts, indicating the amount expected to be collected.

name: Net Receivables Percentage
definitions: Net Receivables Percentage measures the proportion of accounts receivable expected to be collected, calculated as 100% minus the allowance for doubtful accounts percentage. It reflects credit risk and collection efficiency in receivables management.

name: Net Rental Income
definitions: Net rental income refers to the actual profit obtained from renting out a property after deducting all related operating expenses and losses. It is typically calculated by subtracting vacancy losses, rental delinquency losses, and operating costs such as property management, maintenance, and taxes from the gross rental income.

name: Net Rental Income of Owner-occupied Dwellings
definitions: Net rental income of owner-occupied dwellings refers to the implied net income that individuals or households receive by owning and occupying their own homes without paying market rent. In national economic accounting, it is treated as imputed income, used to measure the value of housing services provided by owner-occupied housing. Its calculation is typically based on the market rent of comparable properties minus relevant imputed operating costs (such as depreciation, maintenance expenses, etc.).

name: Net Repayment of Interest-bearing Debt
definitions: Net repayment of interest-bearing debt refers to the difference between the total principal amount of interest-bearing debt repaid and the total amount of newly borrowed interest-bearing debt by a company during a specific period. It is a composite financial metric used in calculating indicators such as Free Cash Flow to Equity.

name: Net Residual Value of Intangible Assets
definitions: The net residual value of an intangible asset refers to the amount, net of estimated disposal costs, that an entity expects to obtain from the disposal of the asset at the end of its estimated useful life. According to accounting standards, the net residual value of an intangible asset with a finite useful life is generally assumed to be zero, unless there is a commitment by a third party to purchase the asset at the end of its life, or unless there is an active market from which the residual value can be determined based on market information.

name: Net Revenue from Principal Operations
definitions: Net revenue from principal operations refers to the net amount of income generated from a company's core business activities during the current period, after deducting sales discounts and allowances. It is a key figure for calculating efficiency metrics such as total asset turnover and is typically sourced from the income statement.

name: Net Sales
definitions: Net sales refers to the total revenue actually obtained by an enterprise from its principal business activities, such as selling goods and providing services, during a specific period, after deducting sales returns, sales allowances, and sales discounts. It serves as the basis for calculating financial indicators such as asset turnover ratio and cost of sales ratio.

Net sales refers to the net revenue amount after deducting items such as sales allowances, sales returns, and sales discounts from gross sales within a specific accounting period. It is a key fundamental metric for measuring a company's core sales performance and calculating financial indicators such as gross profit and working capital turnover ratio.

name: Net Sales Revenue
definitions: Net sales revenue refers to the actual revenue earned by an enterprise from its principal business activities, such as selling goods and providing services, during a specific accounting period. It equals the gross sales revenue minus sales discounts and allowances, as well as sales returns. It serves as the basis for calculating key financial indicators such as accounts receivable turnover ratio and asset turnover ratio.

Net sales revenue refers to the net amount obtained by an enterprise from its principal operating activities, such as selling goods or providing services, within a specific period, after deducting sales returns, sales discounts, and sales allowances. It is a key financial metric for measuring the scale of a company's core business income and is commonly used in calculating financial ratios such as total asset turnover and net profit margin.

name: Net Sales Revenue of Previous Period
definitions: Net sales revenue of the previous period refers to the total revenue earned by an enterprise from selling goods or providing services during the last accounting period (such as the previous year or quarter), after deducting items such as sales discounts, sales allowances, and sales returns incurred during that period. It reflects the actual results of the enterprise's sales activities in the previous period and serves as the base data for calculating financial metrics such as the accounts receivable turnover ratio of the previous period.

name: Net Salvage Value Rate
definitions: Net salvage value rate is a financial metric that measures the proportion of an asset's residual value (after deducting disposal costs) to its original acquisition cost at the end of its estimated useful life, commonly used for depreciation calculation.

name: Net Salvage Value of Fixed Assets
definitions: Net salvage value of fixed assets refers to the net amount of the estimated residual value recoverable by the enterprise at the end of the asset's estimated useful life, minus the estimated disposal costs. It represents the estimated net realizable value of the asset upon retirement.

name: Net Tangible Assets
definitions: Net tangible assets represent the value of a company's tangible asset base after deducting total liabilities and removing intangible assets such as goodwill. It indicates the residual value attributable to physical and other tangible assets, reflecting the firm's tangible net worth.

name: Net Tangible Assets per Share
definitions: Net Tangible Assets per Share measures the tangible book value attributable to common shareholders on a per-share basis. It is calculated by dividing net tangible assets (total shareholders' equity minus intangible assets and sometimes preferred equity) by the number of common shares outstanding, providing a per-share indicator of tangible value.

name: Net Tax Liability or Refund (After Tax Credit)
definitions: Net Tax Liability or Refund (After Tax Credit) represents the resulting tax payable or refund amount after applying tax credits to the initial tax liability. Refundable tax credits can reduce liability below zero and generate a refund, while nonrefundable credits can only reduce liability to a minimum of zero.

name: Net Taxable Income After Capital Gain-Loss Offset
definitions: Net Taxable Income After Capital Gain-Loss Offset represents the taxable amount remaining after capital losses are applied to offset capital gains, with any excess loss deduction constrained by the maximum deductible loss permitted against ordinary income under applicable tax regulations.

name: Net Taxes on Production
definitions: Net taxes on production refer to the net amount of various taxes, surcharges, and fees levied by the government on enterprises or production units during the reporting period for their production, sales, and operating activities, after deducting production subsidies. It reflects the share of primary income obtained by the government from the value added created in the current period and is a key component in calculating value added.

name: Net Transfer Income
definitions: Net transfer income refers to the net amount of total transfer income received by residents or households from the government, enterprises, other institutions, or households during the reporting period, after deducting total transfer payments made externally. It is a key component in calculating disposable income.

name: Net Unrealized Appreciation (NUA)
definitions: Net Unrealized Appreciation (NUA) is the increase in value of employer securities held within a qualified retirement plan above their cost basis. Under the NUA strategy, at a qualifying distribution, the cost basis portion is subject to ordinary income tax, while the NUA portion may be eligible for long-term capital gains tax treatment when the shares are subsequently sold. The provided computation estimates the total tax liability assuming the NUA portion is taxed at capital gains rates and the cost basis is taxed at ordinary income rates.

name: Net Volume
definitions: Net Volume is a technical analysis indicator that measures the difference between the volume traded on price upticks and the volume traded on price downticks, indicating the balance of buying versus selling pressure. A positive Net Volume suggests bullish sentiment, while a negative Net Volume suggests bearish sentiment.

Net volume is a technical analysis indicator calculated as the difference between uptick volume and downtick volume over a period, used to gauge market buying versus selling pressure and overall bullish or bearish sentiment.

name: Net Weight per Unit
definitions: Net weight per unit refers to the actual physical weight of an individual product after removing all packaging materials, containers, or other non-product substances. It is a fundamental physical attribute of the product, typically obtained through direct measurement rather than calculated via financial formulas.

name: Net Working Capital
definitions: Net working capital is the difference between a company's current assets and current liabilities, used to measure its short-term liquidity and solvency. This indicator reflects, in absolute terms, the scale of net current assets invested to maintain normal operations; a larger value typically indicates stronger short-term debt repayment capacity.

name: Net Working Capital Investment in the Final Forecast Period
definitions: Net working capital investment in the final forecast period refers to the projected net working capital amount at the end of the last period (e.g., Year 5) within a defined forecast timeframe (e.g., the next 5 years) in business valuation or project investment analysis. It typically equals the difference between operating current assets (such as accounts receivable and inventory, excluding excess cash) and operating current liabilities (such as accounts payable and accrued expenses) at the end of that period, reflecting the net liquid capital required to maintain normal operations at the forecast horizon.

name: Net Working Capital in Old State
definitions: In capital budgeting or project investment decisions, this specifically refers to the net working capital that a company needs to invest in or occupy in order to maintain the existing (old) operating state before the project begins or before equipment replacement decisions. It is typically used to calculate the net occupancy of current assets and current liabilities when continuing to use old equipment or maintain the old business model, and is an important component in calculating relevant cash flows.

name: Net Worth
definitions: Net worth, also known as net assets, is the residual value after subtracting total liabilities from total assets. It represents the actual wealth level of an enterprise or individual and is a core indicator for measuring solvency and financial strength.
Net worth represents the residual value of an individual's or entity's assets after deducting all liabilities, reflecting the actual wealth owned at a specific point in time.

Net worth represents the difference between an individual's total assets and total liabilities, indicating the residual value that would remain if all debts were settled. It is a core measure of personal financial position and overall wealth.

Net worth represents the residual value of an individual’s or entity’s assets after deducting all liabilities. It reflects financial position at a specific point in time and indicates the capacity to absorb obligations.
Net worth represents the difference between total assets and total liabilities for an individual or entity at a specific point in time, indicating overall financial position and stability.

name: Net of Tax
definitions: Net of tax refers to the amount remaining after deducting taxes from a gross amount, commonly used to assess income, profit, or cash flows after accounting for tax expenses.

name: Net-Net Working Capital
definitions: Net-Net Working Capital (NNWC) is a conservative, liquidation-oriented measure popularized in deep value investing that estimates a company’s residual value by applying haircuts to certain current assets and subtracting total liabilities. It assigns reduced realizable values to accounts receivable and inventory to reflect potential collection and liquidation risk.

name: Netback
definitions: Netback is a per-barrel profitability metric in the oil and gas industry, calculated as the sales price per barrel minus royalties, production costs, and transportation costs. It approximates gross margin per barrel and is a non-GAAP operating measure used to assess upstream operational efficiency and cost competitiveness.

name: Netting
definitions: Netting is the process of offsetting reciprocal financial obligations to determine a single net amount payable or receivable, thereby reducing gross settlement flows, counterparty exposure, and operational complexity. In bilateral netting, a party’s receivables and payables with a single counterparty are offset to one net payment. In multilateral netting, obligations among multiple parties are aggregated and offset to produce net balances for each participant, often used in treasury centers, clearing systems, and derivatives operations.

name: New Accounts Receivable Amount
definitions: New accounts receivable amount refers to the total amount of newly added accounts receivable during a specific accounting period, arising from business activities such as sales of goods or provision of services for which customers have not yet made payment. It reflects the growth of credit sales during that period.

name: New Borrowing Amount
definitions: New borrowing amount refers to the planned incremental loan amount that an enterprise intends to obtain to meet its working capital needs, typically referring to the incremental working capital loan facility. It can be calculated using financial indicators such as working capital requirement, the borrower's own funds, existing working capital loans, and working capital provided through other channels.

name: New Capital Investment
definitions: New capital investment refers to the initial cash outflow required by a company for new assets or investment projects. It is typically calculated based on factors such as capital expenditures, changes in net working capital, proceeds from the sale of old assets, and related tax liabilities, and is a key concept in capital budgeting and intrinsic value assessment.

name: New Cash Discount Rate
definitions: The new cash discount rate refers to a newly established or adjusted price reduction percentage offered by a company to customers for early payment within a specified period, based on the original credit policy, in order to accelerate collection of receivables and improve cash flow. It is typically expressed in the format 'discount rate/payment period', such as '2/10, n/30', meaning the customer can enjoy a 2% price discount if payment is made within 10 days.

name: New Debt
definitions: New debt refers to the incremental increase in debt over a specific period, calculated by comparing the total debt at the beginning and end of the period. It is a key composite metric in financial analysis used to measure changes in debt and assess a company's financing activities, and can be derived from the balance sheet or cash flow statement.

name: New Debt Borrowings
definitions: New debt borrowings refer to the debt formed by funds newly raised or borrowed by an enterprise or entity within a specific period through channels such as banks, financial institutions, or the bond market. It is part of corporate financing activities, used to supplement working capital, undertake capital investments, or repay existing debt.

name: New Debt Issuance
definitions: New debt issuance refers to the total cash proceeds actually raised by a company from investors through the issuance of debt instruments such as bonds in the primary market. This represents a significant cash inflow in the company's financing activities and is directly recorded in the financing activities section of the cash flow statement.

New debt issuance refers to the act of a company or government raising new debt capital from external sources through methods such as bond issuance or bank borrowing. This is an important form of corporate financing, typically used to supplement working capital, fund project investments, or repay existing debt.

name: New Earnings Per Share After Buyback
definitions: New earnings per share (EPS) after a company repurchases a portion of its outstanding shares, calculated by adjusting the pre-buyback EPS for the reduction in share count.

name: New Enterprise Value
definitions: New Enterprise Value refers to the present value of future cash flows brought to investors under improved management and operational strategies after corporate control changes or restructuring, or the overall enterprise value calculated based on post-restructuring financial data. It is a composite metric used to evaluate control premium, representing the value attainable by controlling investors, distinct from the current enterprise value.

name: New Fixed Capital Investment
definitions: New fixed capital investment refers to the additional cash outflow incurred by an enterprise within a specific period (such as a project or a fiscal year) to acquire, construct, or upgrade long-term tangible assets (e.g., plants, equipment, land). It typically constitutes a significant component of the initial project investment or capital budgeting decisions, aimed at expanding production capacity, replacing obsolete equipment, or implementing technological upgrades.

name: New Highs-Lows Ratio
definitions: The New Highs-Lows Ratio is a market breadth indicator that measures the number of stocks hitting new 52-week highs relative to those hitting new 52-week lows, used to assess overall market sentiment and potential reversal points.

name: New Highs-New Lows Ratio
definitions: The New Highs-New Lows Ratio measures the number of securities hitting new highs relative to those hitting new lows, serving as a breadth indicator to gauge overall market strength or weakness.

name: New Interest-bearing Debt
definitions: New interest-bearing debt refers to the increase in a company's total interest-bearing debt during a specific period compared to the previous period. It reflects the additional financing scale obtained by the company through increasing interest-bearing liabilities (such as long-term loans, bonds payable, etc.) and is a key intermediate variable for calculating metrics like Free Cash Flow to Equity.

name: New Price
definitions: New price refers to the transaction price reset for goods, services, or assets after changes in market conditions, cost structures, competitive strategies, or policies. It is typically used to reflect the latest market conditions or corporate decisions and serves as the basis for calculating price change percentages.

name: New Product Development
definitions: New Product Development in finance refers to the total cost or total investment incurred by an enterprise for launching new products, including expenditures in stages such as research and development, design, testing, and market introduction, used for financial evaluation, return on investment calculation, and project decision-making.

name: New Program Peak Activity Level
definitions: New Program Peak Activity Level refers to the highest level of business activity expected or actually achieved after implementing a new business program or plan. In financial management, particularly in cost behavior analysis (such as the high-low method) or program comparison, this metric is often used as a key data point to calculate or evaluate costs, revenues, or profitability under the new program.

name: New Sales Level
definitions: The new sales level is a projected or adjusted sales metric calculated based on benchmark sales data by considering factors such as sales growth rate, discount policy adjustments, or other market factors. It is commonly used in financial forecasting, cash discount cost analysis, and sales performance evaluation.

name: New Sales Revenue
definitions: New sales revenue refers to the revenue generated for the first time by an enterprise within a specific period through the sale of products or services to new customers, or through the sale of new products/services. It excludes repeat purchases or renewal income from existing customers and is a key metric for measuring a company's market expansion capability and growth potential.

New sales revenue refers to the revenue newly generated from operating activities such as selling goods or providing services within a specific accounting period, which has not been recognized in prior periods. It is commonly used to analyze business growth and serves as an important basis for calculating items such as the increase in funds occupied by accounts receivable and the increase in earnings.

name: New Sales Volume
definitions: New sales volume typically refers to the quantity or value of sales that are newly added or exceed the base period level within a specific period (such as a fiscal year or a quarter), used to measure the direct results of business growth and market expansion.

name: New Scheme Highest Activity Level Cost
definitions: New Scheme Highest Activity Level Cost refers to the total cost corresponding to the highest activity level under the new scheme when using the high-low method for cost behavior analysis. It serves as one of the fundamental data points for calculating the unit variable cost and total fixed cost.

name: New Share Issuance
definitions: New share issuance refers to the process in which a company sells its shares to the public for the first time to raise capital. The issue price is a composite indicator determined by comprehensively considering factors such as the company's financial condition, market environment, capital raising needs, and underwriter negotiations, rather than a basic raw data point.

name: New Shareholder Capital Contribution
definitions: New Shareholder Capital Contribution refers to the total amount of funds actually invested by a new investor into the company in exchange for equity ownership, typically through methods such as capital increase and share expansion. These funds are usually used to increase the company's registered capital or capital reserve in return for a corresponding shareholding percentage.

name: New Store Daily Sales
definitions: New store daily sales typically refer to the daily sales revenue generated by a company's newly opened branches, stores, or business units during their initial operating period (especially on the opening day or within the first month). It is often used as a key performance indicator for evaluating the launch effectiveness and initial operational performance of new ventures.

name: New Value
definitions: New Value refers to the net revenue generated by new business, calculated as sales revenue minus direct costs and indirect costs. It is a composite metric commonly used in enterprise valuation and new business value ratio analysis, conforming to the definition of a non-leaf node.

name: Newly Borrowed Interest-bearing Debt
definitions: Newly borrowed interest-bearing debt refers to debt that is newly incurred during a specific accounting period (such as a quarter or a year) and requires interest payments. This includes newly obtained bank loans, newly issued bonds, newly generated finance lease liabilities, etc., but excludes interest-bearing debt that existed and carried over from prior periods. It is an important component when calculating metrics such as 'Net Repayment of Interest-bearing Debt'.

name: Newness Rate
definitions: Newness rate is an indicator reflecting the degree of newness and remaining useful life of an asset, typically expressed as the ratio of the asset's current value to its replacement cost in new condition, used in asset appraisal and financial management.

name: Next Group Frequency
definitions: In grouped statistical data, specifically refers to the frequency of the group immediately following the current group, i.e., the number of occurrences of data within that group.

name: Next Period After-tax Interest Expense
definitions: Next period after-tax interest expense refers to the net amount of a company's interest expense in future periods after considering the impact of income tax, reflecting the actual after-tax cost of the company's debt financing.

name: Next Period Amortization of Intangible Assets
definitions: Next period amortization of intangible assets refers to the amount to be allocated to profit or loss in the next accounting period (typically monthly) for finite-lived intangible assets under the straight-line method, calculated based on their original cost, estimated net residual value, accumulated impairment provisions, and amortization period.

Next period amortization of intangible assets refers to the estimated amortization expense of intangible assets that an enterprise expects to accrue in the next accounting period (such as the next month, next quarter, or next fiscal year). It is calculated using systematic and reasonable methods (e.g., the straight-line method) based on the cost of the intangible asset, its estimated net residual value, impairment provisions, and remaining useful life, and is used to gradually convert the value of the intangible asset into an expense over its economic life.

name: Next Period Amortization of Long-term Deferred Expenses
definitions: Next Period Amortization of Long-term Deferred Expenses refers to the amortization amount calculated by an enterprise based on accounting policies and relevant contracts or estimates (such as the book value of long-term deferred expenses and the estimated amortization months) that should be included in costs or expenses in the next accounting period (e.g., next month, next quarter, or next year). It is a fundamental data point in accounting used to reflect the consumption of long-term deferred expenses in future periods.

name: Next Period Capital Expenditure
definitions: Next period capital expenditure refers to a company's planned investment expenditure on operating long-term assets (such as fixed assets, intangible assets, etc.) for the upcoming period. It is a key component in forecasting the next period's entity free cash flow and is typically a composite indicator calculated through other financial metrics.

name: Next Period Carrying Value of Assets
definitions: Next period carrying value of assets refers to the value at which an asset is expected to be reported on the balance sheet at the end of the next accounting period (e.g., the next fiscal year or quarter), in accordance with accounting standards. It is typically calculated based on the asset's current or expected original cost, accumulated depreciation (or amortization), and the estimated impairment provision to be recognized, reflecting the projected net amount of the asset at a future point in time.

name: Next Period Cash Cost
definitions: Next period cash cost refers to the costs that a company expects to actually pay in cash during a specific future period (such as the next accounting period or the next phase of a project) for its operating or investment activities. It excludes non-cash expenses such as depreciation and amortization, and is directly related to the company's future cash flow planning and fund arrangement.

name: Next Period Cash Flow
definitions: Next period cash flow refers to the forecasted or estimated value of cash flow for a specific future period (typically the next fiscal year or period). It is a key input variable in business valuation, capital budgeting, and risk premium calculations, usually derived through methods such as the expected cash flow approach or adjustments to accounting profits, rather than directly from historical financial statements.

Next period cash flow refers to the net amount of cash inflows and outflows a company is expected to generate in a specific future period (typically the next accounting period). It is a core concept in business valuation, capital budgeting, and financial forecasting, usually estimated based on historical data, operational plans, and market expectations through methods such as the direct method, indirect method, or expected cash flow method.

name: Next Period Contribution Margin
definitions: Next period contribution margin refers to the expected contribution amount formed by subtracting estimated variable costs from projected sales revenue during a specific future operating period (such as the next month, next quarter, or next fiscal year). It reflects the expected contribution capacity of sales activities in that period to cover fixed costs and generate profits, serving as an important basis for forecasting next period earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT).

name: Next Period Depreciation Expense
definitions: Next period depreciation expense refers to the amount of fixed asset value consumption that an enterprise pre-calculates and plans to accrue for the next accounting period (such as the next month, next quarter, or next fiscal year) based on the estimated useful life, original cost, residual value, and selected depreciation method (e.g., straight-line method, double-declining balance method, sum-of-the-years'-digits method). It is a crucial component of forecasting future non-cash expenses.

name: Next Period Depreciation and Amortization
definitions: Next Period Depreciation and Amortization refers to the depreciation and amortization expenses that an enterprise expects to accrue in the next accounting period, calculated according to established accounting policies (such as the straight-line method) based on the original value of fixed assets and intangible assets, estimated net residual value (or net residual value rate), and estimated useful life. This indicator is a calculable composite metric that directly affects the forecasting and evaluation of next period's entity cash flow.

name: Next Period Dividend
definitions: Next period dividend refers to the amount of cash dividend per share that a company is expected to pay to its common shareholders in the upcoming period (typically the next accounting period). It is the forecasted or declared result of the company's dividend policy and is often used as a known baseline forecast input in financial valuation models, such as the Dividend Discount Model.

Next period dividend refers to the expected per-share cash dividend amount that a company is anticipated to pay to its common shareholders over a specific future period (typically the next fiscal year or quarter). It is a forecasted or assumed value based on the company's dividend policy, historical payment patterns, or management guidance, and is commonly used as the starting point for calculations in stock valuation models such as the Dividend Discount Model.

name: Next Period Dividend Cash Flow
definitions: Next period dividend cash flow refers to the expected cash amount of dividends to be paid in the next period. It is typically calculated based on the current dividend and expected growth rate, or derived from earnings per share and the dividend payout ratio. It is a key input variable in the dividend discount model and perpetual growth rate calculations.

name: Next Period Dividend Per Share
definitions: Next Period Dividend Per Share refers to the forecasted or estimated value of cash dividends that a company is expected to distribute to each common shareholder over a specific future period (typically the next fiscal year). It is a forward-looking metric derived from comprehensive factors such as the company's dividend policy, earnings forecasts, retained earnings plans, and share capital structure, rather than historical financial statement data. It is commonly used in valuation models such as the cost of equity capital.

name: Next Period EBIT
definitions: Next Period EBIT refers to a company's profit before deducting interest expenses and income taxes for a specific future period. It reflects the profitability of the company's core operating activities and is a key metric for calculating free cash flow, evaluating operating performance, and conducting financial leverage analysis.

name: Next Period Earnings
definitions: Next Period Earnings is a forecasted value or calculation step in the income approach to valuation, referring to the expected earnings for the first forecast period after the valuation date. It is typically derived by forecasting future net profit and discounting it, rather than being directly taken from raw financial statement line items.

name: Next Period Earnings Per Share
definitions: Next Period Earnings Per Share is a projected or future period's earnings per share. Its calculation logic is the same as basic earnings per share, relying on metrics such as net profit attributable to ordinary shareholders and the weighted average number of ordinary shares outstanding for calculation. It is a composite indicator.

name: Next Period Equity Cash Flow
definitions: Next period equity cash flow is the cash flow that can be freely distributed to equity investors in the future period. It is a composite indicator calculated based on fundamental data such as net profit, depreciation, capital expenditures, and changes in working capital through formulas, and is used for equity valuation.

name: Next Period Expected Dividend Per Share
definitions: Next Period Expected Dividend Per Share refers to the amount of cash dividend per common share that investors or analysts forecast a company will pay in the next payment cycle (typically the next year). It is a future value estimated based on factors such as the company's current dividend, earnings expectations, and dividend policy, and serves as a key input variable in stock valuation models like the Dividend Discount Model.

name: Next Period Fixed Asset Depreciation
definitions: Next Period Fixed Asset Depreciation refers to the estimated depreciation amount to be charged for fixed assets in the next accounting period (e.g., next month, next quarter, or next year), calculated based on the original value of the enterprise's existing fixed assets, estimated useful life, estimated net residual value, and the selected depreciation method (such as the straight-line method). It is a crucial foundational data point in financial forecasting and budgeting.

name: Next Period Fixed Costs
definitions: Next period fixed costs refer to the costs that a company expects to incur in the next accounting period (such as the next month, quarter, or year) that do not vary with changes in business volume (e.g., production or sales volume). These costs remain relatively stable within the relevant range of business activity, such as rent, administrative salaries, depreciation of fixed assets, and long-term loan interest.

name: Next Period Fixed Operating Costs
definitions: Next period fixed operating costs refer to the operational costs that a company expects to incur in the next operating period (such as the next month, quarter, or year) and that do not vary with changes in business volume (such as production or sales volume). These costs are essential for maintaining the basic operations of the enterprise, such as rent, administrative salaries, and depreciation of fixed assets.

name: Next Period Free Cash Flow
definitions: Next Period Free Cash Flow refers to the estimated residual cash flow that a company is expected to generate in the next accounting or forecast period, after meeting reinvestment needs (such as capital expenditures and increases in working capital), which is available for distribution to all capital providers (creditors and shareholders). It is a key input variable used in business valuation to calculate the present value of the terminal value in the stable growth stage.

Next Period Free Cash Flow is the point-in-time version of Free Cash Flow, referring to the forecasted free cash flow for the next future period. It is used in the Discounted Cash Flow model for business valuation, particularly in conjunction with the perpetual growth rate. It is derived through the calculation of multiple financial metrics, making it a computable composite indicator.

name: Next Period Free Cash Flow to the Firm
definitions: Next Period Free Cash Flow to the Firm is a composite metric calculated based on forecasted future revenues, expenses, capital expenditures, and other fundamental data. It reflects the net cash flow generated from the company's future operating activities. It cannot be obtained directly but must be derived through formulas or models, serving as a core input variable for entity valuation.

name: Next Period Gross Operating Cash Flow
definitions: Next Period Gross Operating Cash Flow refers to the projected gross cash flow generated from operating activities in the next period, calculated using metrics such as after-tax operating revenue, after-tax variable costs, after-tax fixed costs, and depreciation & amortization. It serves as a foundational non-leaf node indicator for calculating the next period's entity free cash flow and is used to assess the enterprise's cash generation capacity from operations in the upcoming period.

name: Next Period Income Tax Rate
definitions: The next period income tax rate refers to the base rate used to calculate income tax expenses for the next accounting period (such as the next fiscal year or quarter), as stipulated by national tax laws or set by the enterprise based on future operational forecasts and budgets. It is a pre-determined policy or forecast parameter, not calculated from current financial data.

name: Next Period Interest Expense
definitions: Next Period Interest Expense refers to the estimated interest cost that a company is expected to incur in a specific future accounting period (such as the next quarter or the next fiscal year) due to the use of external borrowings (e.g., bank loans, bonds). It is a crucial component for forecasting future financial conditions and calculating related profit metrics (such as next period EBIT).

name: Next Period Net Cash Flow from Operating Activities
definitions: Next Period Net Cash Flow from Operating Activities refers to the net amount of cash inflows and outflows generated from a company's operating activities in the future period. It is a key indicator for forecasting future cash liquidity, assessing operating performance, and evaluating financial health, typically calculated from other financial metrics.

name: Next Period Net Debt
definitions: Next Period Net Debt refers to the projected or planned net debt amount that an enterprise expects to hold in the next accounting period (such as the next fiscal quarter or fiscal year). It is commonly used for financial forecasting and budgeting. It represents the difference between financial liabilities and financial assets, reflecting the net debt capital the enterprise plans to invest in production and operations in the future.

name: Next Period Net Operating Profit After Tax
definitions: Next Period Net Operating Profit After Tax (NOPAT) is the forecasted net operating profit after tax for a future period, reflecting a company's operating profitability excluding the impact of financing structure. It serves as the basis for calculating financial metrics such as next period free cash flow to the firm. Its calculation formula is the same as that for NOPAT, i.e., net profit after tax plus after-tax interest expense, or earnings before interest and tax multiplied by (1 minus the income tax rate).

name: Next Period Net Profit
definitions: Next Period Net Profit refers to the final net income generated from both operating and non-operating activities of an enterprise in a specific future accounting period. It is a key indicator for measuring the profitability of the enterprise in the future period. Its calculation logic is the same as that of current period net profit, i.e., deducting income tax expense from total profit, or derived by adding net non-operating income to operating profit and then deducting income tax expense.

name: Next Period Net Profit After Tax
definitions: Next Period Net Profit After Tax refers to the final retained profit after the total profit from business activities in a future specific period (e.g., the next accounting period) is subject to income tax according to regulations. It is a core indicator for measuring a company's future profitability and the distributable earnings available to shareholders.

name: Next Period Non-Cash Expenses
definitions: Next period non-cash expenses refer to costs incurred by an enterprise in a specific future operating period that are not directly paid in cash. They typically consist of accounting allocation items such as depreciation and amortization, and serve as key adjustments for calculating metrics like net cash flow from operating activities in the next period.

name: Next Period Non-operating Income
definitions: Next period non-operating income refers to various revenues expected to occur in the next accounting period (such as the next fiscal year, next quarter, or next month) that are not directly related to the enterprise's daily production and operating activities. Such income is typically incidental or non-recurring, for example, gains from disposal of non-current assets, government grants, inventory surplus gains, donation gains, etc.

name: Next Period Non-operating Net Income
definitions: Next period non-operating net income refers to the net income generated by a company from non-core business activities during a specific future accounting period (such as the next fiscal quarter or fiscal year). It typically arises from activities such as investments, financing, or asset disposals, rather than from the daily sale of goods or provision of services.

name: Next Period Operating Cost
definitions: Next period operating cost refers to the total expenses that an enterprise expects to incur for production activities, such as manufacturing products or providing services, in the next accounting period (e.g., the next fiscal year, quarter, or month), which are attributable to product costs or service costs. It typically includes estimated main business costs and other business costs, and is a key component in forecasting the next period's net operating income.

name: Next Period Operating Expenses
definitions: Next period operating expenses refer to the various expense outlays directly related to daily business operations that an enterprise expects to incur in the next accounting period (such as monthly, quarterly, or annual), primarily including selling expenses, administrative expenses, research and development expenses, and financial expenses, but excluding cost of sales.

name: Next Period Operating Net Income
definitions: Next Period Operating Net Income refers to the net profit obtained by an enterprise through its principal operating activities in a future specific period (e.g., the next accounting period), after deducting all related costs, expenses, and income taxes. It reflects the future profitability of the enterprise's core business and is a key foundational indicator for forecasting the net cash flow from operating activities in the next period.

name: Next Period Operating Profit
definitions: Next period operating profit refers to the profit that a company expects to achieve from its normal business operations in a specific future accounting period (such as the next quarter or the next fiscal year), based on current operating conditions and market expectations. It reflects the anticipated profitability from core business activities after deducting operating costs, taxes, and various period expenses, serving as a key leading indicator for forecasting future net profit and assessing the company's going concern capability.

name: Next Period Operating Revenue
definitions: Next Period Operating Revenue refers to the total revenue a company expects to generate from its principal business activities and other operations in the next accounting period (e.g., next quarter, next fiscal year). It is a crucial indicator for forecasting future operating performance and conducting financial planning.

name: Next Period Sales Revenue
definitions: Next period sales revenue refers to the total revenue a company expects to earn from selling goods or providing services in the next accounting period (e.g., next month, next quarter, or next fiscal year). It serves as a crucial basis for sales budgeting and cash flow forecasting.

name: Next Period Variable Cost
definitions: Next period variable cost refers to costs that change in direct proportion to changes in business volume (such as production or sales volume) during the next accounting period or budget period. It serves as a crucial foundational data point for forecasting financial metrics such as EBIT for the upcoming period.

name: Next Quarter Sales Volume
definitions: Next quarter sales volume refers to the forecasted or planned quantity of product sales for the upcoming financial quarter, serving as fundamental data for preparing sales budgets and operating budgets.

name: Next-In, First-Out (NIFO) Profit
definitions: NIFO Profit measures margin under the Next-In, First-Out inventory valuation convention, where the cost of goods sold is based on the current replacement cost (i.e., the cost of the next unit to be acquired) rather than the historical cost. It is used primarily for internal managerial analysis, especially during inflationary periods, and is not permitted under GAAP or IFRS for external financial reporting.

name: Nominal Effective Exchange Rate
definitions: The Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER) is the trade-weighted average of a domestic currency’s bilateral exchange rates against a basket of foreign currencies. Weights reflect the relative trade shares with partner countries. NEER is not adjusted for inflation differentials and serves as an indicator of a currency’s nominal external competitiveness.

name: Nominal GDP
definitions: Nominal GDP refers to the total market value of all final goods and services produced in an economy, measured using current-year (or current-period) market prices. This indicator reflects both changes in the total output of the economy and changes in the price level, serving as a nominal value measure of the total economic activity scale of a country or region over a specific period.

Nominal GDP measures the total monetary value of all finished goods and services produced within a country’s borders in a specific time period, calculated at current market prices without adjusting for inflation.

name: Nominal GDP for the Reporting Period
definitions: Nominal GDP for the reporting period refers to the total market value of all final goods and services produced within a country or region during a specific period (typically a quarter or a year), calculated at current market prices. It does not exclude the effects of price changes (inflation or deflation) and directly reflects the scale of total economic output measured at current prices.

name: Nominal Goods and Services Value
definitions: Nominal goods and services value refers to the total value of all final goods and services calculated at current market prices within a given period, without removing the effects of price changes (inflation or deflation).

name: Nominal Gross Domestic Product
definitions: Nominal Gross Domestic Product is the gross domestic product calculated at current market prices, reflecting the total market value of all final goods and services produced by resident units in a country or region during a given period, which can be measured using the income approach, expenditure approach, or production approach.

name: Nominal Gross Domestic Product (GDP)
definitions: Nominal Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the aggregate market value of all final goods and services produced within an economy during a specific period measured at current prices, unadjusted for inflation. It can be derived by multiplying real GDP by the GDP deflator, a price index that reflects the change in the overall price level relative to a base year.

name: Nominal Growth Amount
definitions: Nominal growth amount (or nominal growth rate) refers to the absolute or relative change in an indicator (such as Gross Domestic Product) calculated at current market prices between two periods. It reflects the growth in nominal value without removing the effects of price changes and is an important composite indicator for measuring changes in the monetary value of economic activity.

name: Nominal Growth Rate
definitions: The nominal growth rate is a ratio measuring the magnitude of change in nominal values from the base period to the reporting period, calculated via formulas rather than from original accounting line items, commonly used to analyze changes in economic or financial indicators such as disposable income

Nominal growth rate is a method of measuring the growth of economic or financial indicators, calculated directly using the nominal values (without adjusting for price changes) of the current period compared to the previous period, reflecting the apparent growth change of the indicator.

name: Nominal Income
definitions: Nominal income refers to the total income of an individual or enterprise over a specific period, calculated in current monetary units (without inflation adjustment). It reflects the absolute monetary amount of income but does not account for the impact of price level changes on purchasing power.

name: Nominal Income Growth Rate
definitions: Nominal income growth rate refers to the rate of increase or change in the total income of an individual or enterprise over a specific period, measured at current monetary value without adjusting for inflation.

name: Nominal Interest Rate
definitions: The nominal interest rate is the rate published by central banks or other lending institutions that has not been adjusted for inflation. It is typically composed of the real interest rate, expected inflation rate (or price change rate), and various risk premium rates.

name: Nominal Interest Rate (Taylor Rule)
definitions: The Nominal Interest Rate (Taylor Rule) is a monetary policy guideline that sets the policy nominal rate as the sum of the target real interest rate, the current inflation rate, and 1.5 times the inflation gap (the deviation of actual inflation from the target inflation rate). This simplified specification guides central banks in adjusting interest rates to stabilize inflation.

name: Nominal Net Exports of Goods and Services
definitions: Nominal net exports of goods and services refer to the difference between the total value of goods and services exported and the total value imported by a country or region during a specific period, calculated at current market prices. It is a core indicator for measuring the balance of trade in goods and services under the current account in the balance of payments.

name: Nominal Rate of Return
definitions: Nominal rate of return is the percentage increase in the value of an investment over a period before adjusting for inflation, taxes, fees, or other costs.

name: Nominal Rate of Return on Stocks
definitions: The nominal rate of return on stocks refers to the investment return calculated solely based on stock price changes and cash dividends (e.g., dividends) during the investor's holding period, without considering the erosion of monetary purchasing power by inflation. It reflects the book-based, unadjusted-for-price-level performance of the investment.

name: Nominal Risk-Free Rate
definitions: The nominal risk-free rate refers to the idealized interest rate that can be obtained by investing in an asset with no default risk or reinvestment risk (such as short-term government bonds), without considering inflation factors. It is a theoretical benchmark rate that is not adjusted for changes in the purchasing power of money.

name: Nominal Total Exports of Goods and Services
definitions: Nominal total exports of goods and services refer to the aggregate market value of all goods and services sold abroad by a country or region within a specific period (typically one year), calculated at current prices without adjusting for price changes (inflation or deflation). It is a key macroeconomic indicator for measuring the scale of a country's external economy and trade activities.

name: Nominal Total Imports of Goods and Services
definitions: Nominal total imports of goods and services refer to the total value of all goods and services purchased from foreign countries by a nation or region during a specific period (typically a year or a quarter), calculated at current market prices. It reflects the total scale of imports without considering price changes (i.e., inflation or deflation) and serves as a key indicator for measuring a country's external economic linkages and demand.

name: Nominal Value for the Reporting Period
definitions: Nominal value for the reporting period refers to the original or base data value within a specific reporting period, without any adjustments (such as removing price change factors). It typically serves as the starting point and reference benchmark for calculating other derived indicators (e.g., real growth rate, real interest rate).

name: Nominal Yield
definitions: Nominal yield refers to the ratio of the coupon interest income of an investment (such as a bond) to its face value (or principal), without considering the impact of factors such as inflation, taxes, or market price fluctuations on real purchasing power. It reflects the nominal return level of the investment.
Nominal yield is the annual interest income divided by the bond's face value, expressed as a percentage, representing the fixed return relative to par regardless of market price fluctuations.

name: Non-Accredited Investor
definitions: A non-accredited investor is an individual who does not meet the SEC's accredited investor thresholds—generally a net worth of at least $1,000,000 excluding the primary residence, or annual income of $200,000 (or $300,000 jointly with a spouse) in each of the past two years with a reasonable expectation of the same—thereby not qualifying for certain private securities offerings under Regulation D.

name: Non-Cash Expenses
definitions: Non-cash expenses refer to costs incurred during the operating period that are not paid in cash, typically including depreciation of fixed assets, amortization of intangible assets, amortization of start-up costs, and interest expenses on borrowings incurred during the operating period under the full investment assumption.

Non-cash expenses are costs incurred by a company during its operating period that are not paid in cash, typically including depreciation of fixed assets, amortization of intangible assets, amortization of start-up costs, and interest expenses on loans incurred during the operating period under the full investment assumption.

Non-cash expenses refer to costs or expenses incurred in business operations that do not directly result in an outflow of cash in the current period but must be deducted when calculating profit. They typically include depreciation, amortization, and interest expense on borrowings under the full investment assumption, and serve as important adjustments for calculating metrics such as net cash flow from operating activities.

Non-cash expenses refer to costs incurred in business operations that do not directly result in cash outflows in the current period but must be recognized in the income statement, primarily including depreciation, amortization, and certain interest expenses. They are significant add-back items used to adjust net profit to cash flow from operating activities when calculating metrics such as free cash flow.

Non-cash expenses refer to costs or expenses incurred by a company in its operating activities that do not require an immediate cash outlay. These expenses are recognized in accounting as costs, thereby reducing current period profits, but do not result in an outflow of cash from the company.

name: Non-Cash Expenses in the Final Forecast Period
definitions: Non-cash expenses in the final forecast period refer to expenses that are recognized in the income statement for the last period (e.g., Year 5) of a defined forecast timeframe (e.g., the next 5 years) in a corporate financial forecast or valuation model, but do not directly result in an outflow of cash in that period. Although these expenses reduce accounting profit, they do not consume cash; therefore, they must be added back to net profit when calculating the operating cash flow for the final period. Common non-cash expenses include depreciation, amortization, and asset impairment provisions.

name: Non-Current Asset Turnover Days
definitions: Non-current asset turnover days represent the average number of days required for a company's non-current assets to complete one turnover cycle, used to evaluate the utilization efficiency of long-term assets.

name: Non-Current Assets to Revenue Ratio
definitions: The Non-Current Assets to Revenue Ratio reflects the proportion of a company's non-current assets relative to its sales revenue, indicating the extent to which long-term assets support business operations.

name: Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF)
definitions: A Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) is a cash-settled forward contract on a currency where physical delivery is restricted or impractical. At settlement, the difference between the agreed NDF rate and the prevailing spot rate is multiplied by the notional amount and settled in a convertible currency, typically USD, without exchanging principal.

name: Non-Deliverable Swap (NDS)
definitions: A Non-Deliverable Swap (NDS) is a cash-settled derivative contract in which counterparties exchange cash flows based on the difference between a contracted exchange rate and the prevailing spot rate at fixing, without physical delivery of the underlying currencies. The net settlement amount is typically paid in a settlement currency (e.g., USD).

name: Non-Liquid Equity Value
definitions: Non-liquid equity value refers to the value of the portion of a company's equity that cannot be freely traded on the open market or is subject to trading restrictions. It is typically calculated as a composite metric based on liquid equity value, net assets, or other financial data through liquidity discount adjustments or valuation methods, and is used to analyze the value of non-tradable shares or restricted equity.

name: Non-Qualified Stock Option (NSO)
definitions: A Non-Qualified Stock Option (NSO) is an equity compensation instrument granting the right to purchase employer stock at a specified exercise (strike) price. Upon selling shares acquired via NSOs, the capital gain or loss equals the difference between the sale price per share and the exercise price per share, multiplied by the number of shares sold. Tax treatment may classify the result as short-term or long-term based on the holding period after exercise, although specific tax rates are not applied in this calculation.

name: Non-Qualified Stock Option (NSO) Compensation Income
definitions: NSO compensation income is the taxable compensation recognized upon exercising non-qualified stock options, equal to the bargain element: the difference between the stock’s market price at exercise and the exercise price, multiplied by the number of shares. It is subject to ordinary income and payroll taxes and typically included in wages.

name: Non-Refundable Tax Credit
definitions: A non-refundable tax credit reduces a taxpayer's income tax liability but cannot reduce it below zero. Non-refundable credits are applied before refundable credits; any remaining tax liability after non-refundable credits may be further offset by refundable credits, which can generate a refund if they exceed the remaining tax liability.

name: Non-Taxable Distribution
definitions: A non-taxable distribution, commonly known as a return of capital, is a payment to shareholders that is not immediately taxable because it represents a return of invested principal rather than income. Such distributions reduce the investor's cost basis in the security. The adjusted cost basis cannot be reduced below zero; any distribution amount that exceeds the remaining basis is treated as a capital gain when received or recognized upon disposition.

name: Non-Taxable Revenue
definitions: Non-taxable revenue refers to income items that, according to tax law provisions, are not derived from a company's profit-making activities in nature and origin, and therefore are not subject to tax obligations nor included as components in calculating the taxable income for corporate income tax purposes.

name: Non-Value-Added Cost of Value-Added Activities
definitions: Non-value-added cost of value-added activities refers to the additional cost incurred in value-added activities due to actual activity output exceeding standard output, typically caused by inefficiencies.

name: Non-cash Revenue
definitions: Non-cash revenue refers to income recognized by an enterprise during an accounting period but not actually received in cash. It is typically recorded based on the accrual accounting principle, reflecting economic benefits earned by the enterprise that have not yet been received in cash, such as accounts receivable from credit sales, accrued interest, etc.

name: Non-cash Sales
definitions: Non-cash sales refer to transactions where a company sells goods or provides services without directly receiving cash, but instead receives other non-monetary assets (such as inventory, fixed assets) or equity interests (such as receivables, equity), or completes sales through debt settlement, exchange, or similar arrangements. Such transactions do not directly generate cash inflows and require special attention when analyzing a company's cash flow.

name: Non-controlling Interest
definitions: Non-controlling interest refers to the portion of equity in a subsidiary's consolidated financial statements that is not attributable to the parent company (i.e., the controlling shareholder). It represents the share of the subsidiary owned by other investors.

name: Non-current Asset Turnover Ratio
definitions: The non-current asset turnover ratio measures a company's ability to support operating revenue with its non-current assets over a specific period, reflecting the utilization efficiency of long-term assets.

name: Non-current Assets
definitions: Non-current assets refer to assets that an enterprise expects to hold for more than one year or one normal operating cycle, and are not intended or cannot be converted into cash, sold, or consumed in the short term. These assets typically require substantial capital investment, have slow turnover rates, and relatively poor liquidity, forming the foundation for long-term operations and investments of the enterprise.

name: Non-current Assets Due within One Year
definitions: Non-current assets due within one year refer to the amount of non-current assets held by an enterprise that are expected to be realized or recovered within one year (including one year) from the balance sheet date. It mainly includes held-to-maturity investments due within one year, long-term prepaid expenses, and long-term receivables recoverable within one year. The amount of this item is directly analyzed and filled in based on the ending balances of relevant accounting accounts and is a specific item on the balance sheet.

name: Non-current Assets Due within One Year (Previous Period)
definitions: Non-current assets due within one year (previous period) refers to the amount of non-current asset items that, as of the balance sheet date of the prior reporting period (e.g., the previous fiscal year or quarter), were expected to mature, be realized, or be collected within one year (including one year). It reflects the portion of long-term assets that, at the end of the prior period, were about to be converted into current assets or cash in the short term.

name: Non-current Liabilities
definitions: Non-current liabilities refer to debts that a company is required to repay after more than one year or one normal operating cycle (whichever is longer). They represent long-term funding sources raised by the enterprise to support long-term development, such as purchasing equipment or expanding facilities.

name: Non-current Liabilities Due within One Year (Prior Period)
definitions: Non-current liabilities due within one year (prior period) refer to the portion of long-term liabilities (with a repayment period exceeding one year) that were scheduled to mature and require repayment within the 12 months following the financial statement date of the previous accounting period (e.g., the prior year or prior quarter). This portion of liabilities was classified as current liabilities in the prior period.

name: Non-deductible Input VAT
definitions: Non-deductible input VAT refers to the value-added tax paid or borne by an enterprise when purchasing goods, services, intangible assets, or real estate, which, according to tax regulations, cannot be credited against output VAT and must instead be included in the cost of the relevant assets or recognized as current period expenses. This commonly occurs in purchase transactions related to tax-exempt items, simplified tax calculation projects, collective welfare, or personal consumption.

name: Non-deductible Sales Revenue for the Current Period
definitions: Non-deductible sales revenue for the current period refers to that portion of a company's sales income during a specific tax period for which the corresponding input VAT cannot be credited against output VAT, as stipulated by tax laws. This typically occurs when selling tax-exempt items, items subject to the simplified tax calculation method, or goods or services used for non-taxable purposes such as collective welfare or personal consumption.

name: Non-interest-bearing Long-term Liabilities
definitions: Non-interest-bearing long-term liabilities refer to long-term debts with a repayment period exceeding one year, as presented on the balance sheet, for which no interest payments are required during the debt's tenure according to relevant contracts or agreements. They are typically fundamental line items directly identifiable from financial statement accounts, such as the amount of long-term payables excluding the interest-bearing portion.

name: Non-operating Assets
definitions: Non-operating assets refer to assets not directly used in a company's core business operations. They are typically not primary line items in financial statements and are calculated by subtracting total operating assets from total assets or by aggregating specific non-operating asset accounts. They are used in invested capital analysis to isolate core business value.

name: Non-operating Assets Adjustment
definitions: Non-operating Assets Adjustment is an adjustment item applied to total assets in enterprise valuation or financial analysis to calculate adjusted total assets. It is determined by identifying and summing asset items held by the enterprise that are unrelated to its core business or not essential for ongoing operations (such as excess cash, idle assets, investment properties, etc.), making it a composite analytical metric.

name: Non-operating Assets such as Financial Investments
definitions: Non-operating assets such as financial investments refer to financial assets held by an enterprise not for daily production and operating activities, with the primary purpose of obtaining investment returns, capital appreciation, or meeting strategic investment needs, rather than directly serving the core business. Such assets typically include trading financial assets, other equity instrument investments, debt investments, etc.

name: Non-operating Expenses
definitions: Non-operating expenses refer to various expenditures incurred by an enterprise outside its main business activities that are not directly related to daily operations. They typically include non-operating expenses, financial expenses, etc., and are used to calculate non-operating net income or to adjust net operating income.

Non-operating expenses refer to various expenditures incurred by an enterprise outside its normal operating activities that are not directly related to its main business. They are typically considered as components in calculating non-operating net income or non-recurring gains and losses, and affect the calculation of operating profit.

Non-operating expenses refer to various expenditures incurred by an enterprise outside its daily operating activities that are not directly related to its main business, such as fines, compensation payments, losses on asset disposals, and donation expenses. These expenses typically do not occur frequently and do not constitute the cost of the enterprise's core operations.

Non-operating expenses refer to various costs or losses incurred by an enterprise outside its daily business operations, which are not directly related to the production or sales process of products or services.

name: Non-operating Expenses (Loss on Disposal of Fixed Assets)
definitions: Non-operating Expenses (Loss on Disposal of Fixed Assets) refers to the loss incurred when the disposal proceeds (from sale, scrapping, damage, etc.) of a fixed asset are lower than its carrying amount and related taxes and fees. This loss is not part of the company's ordinary business activities and is therefore recorded as a non-operating expense.

name: Non-operating Expenses for Next Period
definitions: Non-operating expenses for the next period refer to various losses or expenditures that a company expects to incur in the next accounting period (such as the next month, quarter, or year) and are not directly related to its daily production and operating activities.

name: Non-operating Income
definitions: Non-operating income refers to various revenues or gains incurred by an enterprise outside its daily business operations, which are not directly related to its main business activities. It is not generated from selling products or providing routine services, but rather from incidental or special events.
Non-operating income refers to various revenues generated by an enterprise outside its daily business operations that are not directly related to its main business activities.

name: Non-operating Income (Gain on Disposal of Fixed Assets)
definitions: Non-operating Income (Gain on Disposal of Fixed Assets) refers to the net gain obtained by an enterprise from disposing of fixed assets (such as through sale, scrapping, or damage), calculated as the proceeds or disposal price minus the carrying amount of the fixed asset, related taxes and fees, and disposal expenses. This portion of income is not directly related to the enterprise's ordinary operating activities and is therefore recorded as non-operating income.

name: Non-operating Net Income
definitions: Non-operating net income refers to the net amount after offsetting various revenues and expenses that are not directly related to the daily operating activities of an enterprise, reflecting the financial results generated by non-core business activities such as investment and financing activities.

name: Non-operating Net Income and Expenses
definitions: Non-operating net income and expenses refer to the net amount after offsetting various revenues and expenses that are not directly related to normal business operations within a specific accounting period, reflecting the impact of non-operating activities on profit.

name: Non-operating Net Profit
definitions: Non-operating net profit refers to the net income generated by a company from investment activities and financing activities other than its main business (operating activities). It is an important indicator for measuring the profitability of a company's non-core business and is commonly used to calculate comprehensive income metrics such as net operating income.

name: Non-operating Profit
definitions: Non-operating profit refers to the profit earned by a company outside its regular business activities. It is typically derived as a composite metric through formulas rather than being a direct primary data point, for example, derived from net operating income or operating profit.

name: Non-recurring Income Adjustments
definitions: Non-recurring income adjustments refer to income items that need to be excluded from net profit when calculating metrics such as Economic Value Added (EVA). These items are not directly related to the company's core business operations, occur infrequently, or are of a special nature. They typically require identification and aggregation based on the specific substance of the business activities, such as gains from selling high-quality core business assets or reducing stakes in entities with substantive control, to ensure the financial data more accurately reflects the core profitability of the company's ongoing operations.

name: Non-standard Equipment Design Fee
definitions: Non-standard equipment design fee refers to the design service charges collected by designers for specially designed, non-mass-produced equipment that meets specific process requirements. Its billing basis is typically the preliminary design budget estimate or estimated cost of the non-standard equipment, multiplied by the corresponding design fee rate for calculation.

name: Non-standard Equipment Design Fee Rate
definitions: The non-standard equipment design fee rate refers to a percentage coefficient used in asset valuation or engineering cost estimation to calculate the design cost for non-standard equipment (i.e., non-standardized equipment requiring specialized design). This rate is typically determined based on the preliminary design budget estimate (billing amount) of the equipment to ascertain the specific design fee amount.

name: Non-tradable Equity Value
definitions: Non-tradable equity value refers to the value corresponding to shares issued by a company that cannot be freely traded on public markets, typically calculated based on net asset value per share. It is an important concept used to distinguish between tradable and non-tradable portions when assessing a company's overall equity value.

name: Non-tradable Shares
definitions: Non-tradable shares refer to shares in a company's capital structure that, according to relevant laws, regulations, or the company's articles of association, cannot be publicly and freely traded on a stock exchange. These shares typically originate from company establishment, capital increases, or equity incentive programs, and their transfer is subject to specific conditions and procedures.

Non-tradable shares refer to the total number of shares in a company (typically a listed company) that cannot be publicly and freely traded on a stock exchange.
